chunks: Ali, from his father, from one of his companions, from Asim ibn companions, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A Prophet from the Prophets complained to his Lord: 'How can I judge in matters in which I have not been informed of their explanation?' He said, so He said to him: 'Refer them to Me, and add them to My Name to swear by.'
ai.seo_question: How did a Prophet handle judicial matters when specific details were not revealed to him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *al-yamin* (oath) in Islamic jurisprudence, where a Prophet seeks divine guidance for unresolved judicial matters. It highlights the theological significance of invoking God's Name to establish truth when explicit revelation is absent, a concept foundational to Shia legal theory regarding oaths in court. The narrative underscores the continuity between prophetic practice and the authority of the Imams in applying similar judicial mechanisms.
